directive: Valerius orders his men to continue the established household protocols and inspections while treating local residents with respect, and he sends the final completely detailed, chronologically labeled, and confirmed dossier of evidence concerning the raid inquiry.

events.title: VALERIUS ORDERS THE HOUSEHOLD PROTOCOLS TO CONTINUE WITHOUT EXCEPTION
events.body: Valerius gives renewed instructions that the established protocols governing the household and its holdings are to continue without alteration. The men responsible for household security and daily administration are told to conduct their expected inspections, keep watch over the property, and carry out their duties without treating ordinary local residents as presumptive enemies or intruders. The order emphasizes restraint in dealings with people living near the estate and requires those carrying out household duties to speak and act respectfully when dealing with other locals. Estate stewards are reminded that the household's established records and procedures remain in force alongside these expectations of conduct. No new force is raised and no new restriction is imposed upon the surrounding community. The instruction is instead a reaffirmation of the standards already governing Valerius's household as spring activity increases.

events.title: HOUSEHOLD INSPECTIONS CONTINUE UNDER THE ESTABLISHED ROUTINE
events.body: The household men continue their ordinary inspections of the estate and its immediate approaches under the instructions renewed by Valerius. The inspections concern the condition of the holdings, the movement of people and goods through the property, and the proper maintenance of the household's established routines. Those carrying out the work are reminded to distinguish ordinary local activity from conduct that actually requires intervention. Encounters with nearby residents remain governed by the instruction to act respectfully and avoid unnecessary disputes. The work produces no new seizure, arrest, confrontation, or change in the estate's organization. It is a continuation of the household's existing practice as the spring season proceeds.

events.title: THE FINAL EVIDENCE DOSSIER IS SENT TO THE ROMAN CORRESPONDENTS
events.body: Valerius sends the final dossier concerning the earlier raid inquiry through the established Roman correspondence. The dossier is assembled as a complete chronological record, with each item labeled by date and placed in the sequence in which the relevant testimony, correspondence, and supporting material were received or preserved. The scribes identify the sources of the individual statements and distinguish the original records from later copies, while the chronology is checked against the estate's retained correspondence before the packet is sealed. The material concerning Aulus Vettius is included in the same documentary sequence, without adding an accusation that the evidence itself does not establish. Valerius's covering communication makes clear that the dossier is being sent as a complete evidentiary record rather than as a selective account intended to omit inconvenient material. The packet therefore represents the fullest and most carefully organized submission yet made in connection with the inquiry.

events.title: THE ROMAN SIDE ACKNOWLEDGES RECEIPT OF THE COMPLETE RECORD
events.body: Confirmation reaches Valerius that the completed dossier has been received by the Roman correspondents to whom it was addressed. The acknowledgment concerns receipt of the assembled record rather than a final judgment on the underlying inquiry. Valerius's scribes preserve the acknowledgment with the duplicate of the dossier so that the household retains a record of what was sent and when it was received. The inquiry is therefore placed on a more complete documentary footing while the substance of the evidence remains available for whatever consideration follows. No new accusation or public proceeding arises from the acknowledgment itself. For the estate, the immediate task of assembling and transmitting the final chronological record is complete.
